**Sandbox check (step 0):** passed.
- (a) Writing `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-DAEO-k4wm` failed with `OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`, as it should.
- (b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` worked (`1ae28402a109…`), and `git update-index --refresh` worked.

**ps check:** `ps -eo pid,args` shows only the sandbox's own three processes. No ollama or llama-server is mine, and I started no embedder, reranker or model.

- **task:** W2-133 (DAEO-k4wm), the engineer. A narrowed or gap-starting register item carries its own entry's id (DEC-1083).
- **status:** DONE.
- **work_completed:**
  - **`retrieve.py`, the label lines only:** the `id` is now the entry holding the item's first line, found by `entry_of` (`authority.register_entries_of`), with that entry's status fields. An item whose first line is in the preface or a gap keeps its chunk id and carries no entry of its own. Every entry its lines touch goes in `also`, so the status of the entry whose text it holds still travels with it.
  - **`register.leave_out`:** a new inner `narrowed()` drops the parent's `entry`, `status`, `changed_by`, `in_force`, `not_in_force` and `also`. It relabels the item from the narrowed chunk's first line by the same rule. Each entry's status fields are copied from the parent's own per-entry marks, which `retrieve` already computed, so nothing is recomputed or guessed in `register.py`.
  - An item with no status fields (as `supplementary`'s items are) gets its `id` only. Nothing else in a kept item changes.
- **files_changed:**
  - `src/gov/decisions/register.py` (+27/−5)
  - `src/gov/retrieval/retrieve.py` (+9/−7): the source diff is **+36/−12**.
  - `tests/unit/decisions/test_w2_133_narrowed_label.py` (new)
  - `tests/unit/retrieval/test_w2_133_gap_label.py` (new)

  - W2-131's 11 and W2-55's 8 unit tests still pass in the same run (34 passed in all).
  - **`gov accept W2-133`:** pass, **48/48**. success-1 13/13, success-2 6/6, success-3 29/29; 0 unmapped, 0 skipped.
  - **`tests/unit/decisions` and `tests/unit/retrieval`:** 428 passed, 18 failed, 303 deselected.
    - All 18 failures are in `test_w2_112_shared_reranker.py`: the sandbox refuses the shared reranker's Unix socket. They are the same 18 W2-131 recorded, the file never reaches the changed code, and `test_the_socket_is_the_users_alone` is red alone too.
    - The exclusion left out the `local_only` cases and the `real`, `green_here` and `time_limit` cases.
  - Every run went through `heavy_slot.sh`, with `HOME` set to an empty folder that has only `~/.local/lib/python3.12/site-packages` linked in.
- **discoveries:**
  - Today's chunker cuts the register at every level 1–3 heading, so no chunk or parent starts in a gap and runs into an entry, and no parent spans two entries. Both fixes are defensive. The tests plant those cases: a stood-in `lexical.parent` on the retrieval side, planted parent items on the `leave_out` side.
  - Untracked dotfiles appeared at the worktree root (`.bashrc`, `.mcp.json`, `.vscode`, `.idea`, …). They are not mine, probably sandbox mount placeholders. I left them alone and did not commit them.
- **risks:** a gap starter's `also` names every entry it touches. Today that is never more than one, because of the chunker's cuts. If a future chunker made parents span many entries, `also` would grow with them.
- **lessons:** the last chunk of a register section includes the blank line before the next heading. Its `end_line` is the next heading's line minus 1, not the entry's last text line.
- **proposed_decisions:** none. One reading to confirm: S2 says only "carries its chunk id". I read that as a gap starter having no `entry` key, with the entries it touches named in `also`. That keeps W2-131's rule `id == entry or chunk id` and keeps those entries' status in the bundle. The acceptance cases pass with it.
- **unresolved:** the 18 shared-reranker socket reds are for the CTO's scoped run outside the sandbox. S4 is the CTO's after re-pin window 4.
- **recommended_next_action:** the CTO runs the scoped set and the 18 shared-reranker tests outside the sandbox, then the independent review, then merges `w2/W2-133` into `w2/integrate` before re-pin window 4 is built.
